## TL;DR

The pipeline card now gets its complete dev/review round text from one shared formatter. The label reads `D<n> · R<m>`, stays amber for a review that requested changes, and retains the green check or red retry mark when those marks communicate the verdict. A running review shows its upcoming round. Pipeline cards continue to use the same global `.rounds-badge` styles as the task drawer. The sent-back note is absent from the pipeline lane rendering.

## Work and rationale

I reviewed the task specification and the existing implementation in `PipelineView.vue`, `PipelineCard.vue`, `TaskDrawer.vue`, `pipeline-card.ts`, the shared stylesheet, and the pipeline view tests. The worktree already had the main visual wiring in place: lane data used `pipelineRoundLabel`, the card rendered one `.rounds-badge`, and the drawer used the same class with `taskRoundLabel`. The stage template also had no sent-back note. I kept those established pieces rather than introducing another card-specific style or changing the drawer's display.

The remaining drift risk was that `reviewerChip` still returned only an optional reviewer suffix (`✓`, `↻`, or an upcoming `R` label), while `pipelineRoundLabel` independently built the complete D/R label. I changed `reviewerChip` to own the complete badge text, accepting the shared `TaskRoundCounts`, review tone, and running state. `pipelineRoundLabel` delegates to that function, preserving the existing caller API while ensuring the badge label and verdict suffix are formatted together. Amber intentionally adds no words or mark because the pill's color carries the state; green and red keep their compact symbols. A running review with no prior verdict includes the next review count and ellipsis.

I updated the pipeline-card unit tests to cover complete labels for amber, green, red, active review, and a neutral state. The test also checks the compact amber label length, while the existing component test confirms the card uses the shared `rounds-badge` class. I declared the requested Work Queue pipeline screenshot with the badge as its highlight.

## Approaches tried

I considered removing `reviewerChip` as obsolete, since the pipeline currently needs one complete label. I instead made it the canonical full-label formatter because the task specifically calls out its tests and the existing public helper already represents reviewer-specific display logic. Keeping `pipelineRoundLabel` as a delegating wrapper minimizes changes to the view and preserves a descriptive call site.

I also checked whether a bespoke narrower card style was needed. The global badge already enforces `white-space: nowrap`, and the compact combined text is shorter than the former reviewer text. Keeping the shared badge style better satisfies the requirement that card and drawer remain visually aligned.

## Challenges and blockers

The checked-out worktree already contained a substantial implementation of this task before this session, with a clean starting tree and recent WIP checkpoint commits. This meant the necessary work was verification and closure of the remaining formatter/test mismatch rather than rebuilding the UI from scratch. Repository-wide search found unrelated uses of the phrase “sent back” in other contexts, but none in the pipeline view or pipeline card. No external dependency, live account, or human-only verification was needed.

The required scoped RepoOS check remains the decisive validation step for this session. The declared screenshot is captured by the RepoOS handoff process; I have not claimed a visual capture result here.

## Key learnings

The drawer and pipeline can share the data calculation without sharing the whole display function: the drawer intentionally presents plain D/R counts, while the pipeline adds verdict tone and review progress. A small shared formatter boundary handles that difference cleanly. Keeping the round counts, tone mark, and upcoming review number together also makes it harder for a separate reviewer-chip implementation to diverge again.
